# attio/assert

A built-in deliver adapter for person records: it needs the step's `uses:` fields, `email` and declares no fields of its own. Plan prices it at $0 per record, and it demands `ATTIO_API_KEY`.

## Manifest

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| id | `attio/assert` |
| version | 1 |
| role | deliver |
| entity type | person |
| credentials | `ATTIO_API_KEY` |
| cost estimate per record | $0 |

## Needs

```json
{
  "dynamic": true,
  "properties": {
    "email": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "email"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## Provides

Nothing; a delivery row is what it writes.

## Config keys

The keys `with:` accepts. Plan rejects any other key.

| Key | Type | Required | What it sets |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base_url` | string |  | Override the API host (testing) |
| `matching_attribute` | string |  | Attribute Attio matches existing records on |
| `object` | string |  | Attio object slug to assert into |
| `variables` | object |  | Egress mapping, target attribute slug → ledger field (ADR-018). Injected by the runner from the step-level variables: key — never authored inside with:. Each resolved variable becomes an attribute value on the asserted record. |

## Example

A minimal step:

```yaml
  - id: assert
    use: attio/assert
```
